title: Equal catch size gave no clear rainfall slope change for beetle richness in four British samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether equal catch size changed the rainfall link to recorded beetle richness. We used 1,311 selected ten-trap collections in England and Scotland in 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. Models controlled temperature, collection duration and date, location by month, and year. Observed minus 20-individual richness slopes were -0.014, +0.028, +0.026 and +0.075 taxon codes per 1 mm/day. All four adjusted year-cluster intervals included zero. The results do not show a common slope change or prove that capture bias is absent. Coarse country weather, selected complete catches, few Scottish collections and few year clusters limit inference. This follow-up reuses the records and model of a campaign warmth study. It tests rainfall, not weather extremes, air pollution or causal climate change. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and a figure support reproduction. External raw data and record tables remain outside the package.

display.caption: Rainfall slopes for observed and 20-individual richness and their paired difference. Year-cluster t intervals use a four-test correction. Country weather is monthly, not daily observed rain.
